scope: Theorem 8.3 (Two invariant-plane realizations) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 23-24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The neighboring-cell recorder has the following effective zero-data forced Navier–Stokes realizations at fixed positive computable viscosity. Both have all mixed derivatives bounded, period one for t ≥ 1, and uniformly bounded kinetic energy. 23 1. On the unit torus, any tape differing from blank on a specified finite set of cells is allowed. The force is mean zero and general, and the solution is unique in the classical periodic class. The particle from (1/16, 1/16, 0) enters {x : 1/2 < x1 < 7/8} exactly when the machine halts. 2. On R3, for a finite word starting at cell zero, the force is general with one compact spatial support uniform in time. The particle from the origin has negative first coordinate at some time exactly when the machine halts. Uniqueness holds for smooth solutions with bounded velocity on finite intervals and u ∈ CtH2 ∩ C1 t L2, p ∈ CtH1; no bound on the competing velocity gradient is required. The repeated field depends only on the table; only the loader uses the input. Neither force is required to decay or be solenoidal. The same formulas are effective relative to arbitrary fixed real positive viscosity.
